item.title: setup_sprint_environment calls undefined release_lock function
item.intent: When --category yields no items, aishore exits cleanly with code 1 and a clear message — no 'command not found' crash, no fd leak.
item.description: When --category filter yields no ready items, setup_sprint_environment() at line 2706 calls release_lock which is never defined anywhere in the script. With set -euo pipefail this triggers exit code 127 ('command not found') rather than a clean return 1. The user sees a confusing crash instead of the log_warning message that precedes it. The lock fd (9) is released on process exit anyway, so the fix is simply removing the undefined call.
steps: Confirm release_lock is not defined anywhere in .aishore/aishore
At line 2706, remove the release_lock call — the flock on fd 9 is released on process exit and no explicit release is needed here
Verify the early-exit path at lines 2701-2708 returns 1 cleanly after the log_warning
Run: .aishore/aishore run --category nonexistent and confirm exit code is 1 with no 'command not found' in output
shellcheck passes with no new warnings
acceptanceCriteria: Running .aishore/aishore run --category nonexistent returns exit 1 with the category warning, not a command-not-found error
A subsequent .aishore/aishore run succeeds in acquiring the lock normally
